facts.text: The Dorchester is on Park Lane in Mayfair, overlooking Hyde Park, halfway between Buckingham Palace and Marble Arch.
facts.excerpt: It's in the heart of Mayfair: overlooking Hyde Park, halfway between Buckingham Palace and Marble Arch.

facts.text: The Dorchester sits directly opposite Hyde Park, and many rooms and suites have views across the park.
facts.excerpt: The Dorchester sits directly opposite Hyde Park, offering many rooms and suites with views across the park.

facts.text: In 2026 The Dorchester completed a major four-year renovation that refreshed its rooms, suites and public spaces while preserving its historic character.
facts.excerpt: In 2026, The Dorchester completed a major four-year renovation that refreshed its rooms, suites and public spaces while preserving the hotel's historic character.

facts.text: The four-year renovation was the most significant in The Dorchester's history.
facts.excerpt: Following a four-year renovation, the most significant in The Dorchester’s history

facts.text: The rooms and suites are inspired by the colours and motifs of a classic English garden.
facts.excerpt: Inspired by the colours and motifs of a classic English garden, our beautiful rooms and suites invite you to unwind in wonderful comfort.

facts.text: The hotel's butlers are all trained to a royal standard.
facts.excerpt: They're complemented by the impeccable standards of our butlers, all trained to a royal standard.

facts.text: The Royal Suite occupies a corner of the eighth floor above Hyde Park.
facts.excerpt: Occupying a vast corner of the eighth floor, The Royal Suite rises above Hyde Park with a sense of command.

facts.text: The Royal Suite has a 1950s spirit, with pastel tones and floral references taken from Hyde Park.
facts.excerpt: A 1950s spirit runs throughout, with pastel tones and floral references taking their cue from Hyde Park

facts.text: The Royal Suite was designed by Pierre-Yves Rochon.
facts.excerpt: Designed by Pierre-Yves Rochon, the suite blends refined elegance with a welcoming warmth.

facts.text: A portion of each Royal Suite booking is donated to The Royal Parks, the charity that protects London's parks.
facts.excerpt: When you book a stay at The Royal Suite, we’ll donate a portion to The Royal Parks, helping to support the preservation of London’s historic and natural parklands.

facts.text: The Oliver Messel Terrace Suite was designed by Oliver Messel.
facts.excerpt: This suite of suites was designed by Oliver Messel, and is globally adored by a shimmering history of illustrious guests.

facts.text: Selected suites include dedicated butler service, complimentary round-trip airport transfers and use of a chauffeur-driven car subject to availability.
facts.excerpt: Selected suites at The Dorchester include exclusive benefits such as dedicated butler service, complimentary round-trip airport transfers, access to a chauffeur-driven car (subject to availability)

facts.text: Alain Ducasse at The Dorchester holds three Michelin stars.
facts.excerpt: Alain Ducasse at The Dorchester is our three Michelin-starred restaurant in London.

facts.text: Chef patron Jean-Philippe Blondet has worked alongside Alain Ducasse for over a decade.
facts.excerpt: Jean-Philippe Blondet has been working alongside Alain Ducasse for over a decade, interpreting Ducasse’s cuisine in a contemporary and refined way

facts.text: The Grill at The Dorchester serves modern British cuisine.
facts.excerpt: The Grill at The Dorchester serves modern British cuisine in a relaxed, stylish setting.

facts.text: Martyn Nail leads The Grill's culinary direction.
facts.excerpt: Bringing a wealth of experience from 40 years of working at the finest luxury hotels, Martyn Nail helms our culinary direction.

facts.text: The Grill has a copper pudding bar.
facts.excerpt: Sweeping burgundy curtains frame the copper pudding bar.

facts.text: China Tang at The Dorchester is a subterranean restaurant.
facts.excerpt: Stepping into China Tang draws diners deep into a subterranean jewel box of adventure.

facts.text: China Tang serves dim sum all day in its bar.
facts.excerpt: Our dim sum are so delicious, we have to serve them all day in the bar

facts.text: Afternoon tea is served in The Promenade.
facts.excerpt: Afternoon tea is served in The Promenade, one of the hotel's most iconic spaces.

facts.text: In The Promenade, Liberace's piano is played by a resident pianist.
facts.excerpt: Liberace’s famous piano serenades our diners under the skilful hands of our resident pianist.

facts.text: The Promenade's Gibson Trolley brings martinis directly to the table.
facts.excerpt: The Promenade’s Gibson Trolley brings the art of the martini directly to your table.

facts.text: Artists' Bar has a bespoke Lalique crystal bar and mirrored interiors.
facts.excerpt: wonderfully complementing the bespoke Lalique bar and mirrored interiors.

facts.text: Vesper Bar was designed by London interiors specialist Martin Brudnizki.
facts.excerpt: Vesper Bar showcases strikingly beautiful, contemporary design from London’s interiors specialist, Martin Brudnizki.

facts.text: Vesper Bar is adults only.
facts.excerpt: Adults only

facts.text: The Chef's Table is a private dining space inside the hotel's kitchen, seating up to 12 guests.
facts.excerpt: The Chef’s Table is our private dining space, tucked away within our renowned kitchen. With seating for up to 12 guests

facts.text: Parcafe is the hotel's own coffee shop overlooking Hyde Park.
facts.excerpt: Serving artisanal coffee and homemade delights, this is our very own coffee shop, overlooking Hyde Park.

facts.text: Ronnie Scott's brings live jazz to The Grill once a month in 2026.
facts.excerpt: Feel the energy and spirit of live jazz as the renowned Ronnie Scott’s comes to The Grill for 2026. Join us once a month

facts.text: The Dorchester has no pool in the hotel itself; guests can use the indoor pool at sister hotel 45 Park Lane.
facts.excerpt: While The Dorchester does not have a pool within the hotel itself, guests enjoy access to the 20-metre indoor swimming pool at nearby sister property 45 Park Lane.

facts.text: The spa includes treatment rooms, a relaxation room, an MLX Quartz treatment bed and the Carol Joy London hair salon.
facts.excerpt: including treatment rooms, a relaxation room, an MLX Quartz treatment bed, and the Carol Joy London hair salon.

facts.text: The spa offers La Prairie facial treatments.
facts.excerpt: The Dorchester Spa offers exclusive La Prairie facial treatments

facts.text: The hotel has a Carol Joy London hair salon.
facts.excerpt: The hotel is home to the Carol Joy London hair salon

facts.text: Infant cots are complimentary.
facts.excerpt: Infant cots are complimentary

facts.text: Connecting rooms are available for families.
facts.excerpt: offers a range of services and amenities designed for guests travelling with children including connecting rooms.

facts.text: The Dorchester welcomes up to two small dogs for a daily fee.
facts.excerpt: We welcome up to two small dogs (max 7 kg/15 lbs) with a daily fee of £35

facts.text: The hotel asks guests not to wear shorts or sportswear during afternoon tea and in the evening.
facts.excerpt: Guests are kindly asked not to wear shorts or sportswear during afternoon tea service or in the evening.

facts.text: Valet parking is offered for guests and visitors.
facts.excerpt: Yes, The Dorchester offers valet parking for guests and visitors.

facts.text: Advance reservations are recommended for the restaurants and afternoon tea.
facts.excerpt: Advance reservations are recommended for all restaurants and afternoon tea experiences

facts.text: The hotel is about 45 minutes by car from Heathrow Airport, depending on traffic.
facts.excerpt: The Dorchester is approximately 45 minutes by car from Heathrow Airport, depending on traffic conditions.

facts.text: The Dorchester describes itself as London's most storied hotel in Mayfair.
facts.excerpt: Welcome to London’s most storied hotel in Mayfair

facts.text: The hotel calls its spa one of the best in London.
facts.excerpt: Be relaxed or revitalised in one of the best spas in London.
